1.sofaString: 364	Pt, **** *****, is a 16 y/o male with dilated cardiomyopathy and presumed ******'s muscular dystrophy (not confirmed by ******* *******), referred by ******** *******, ****, Transplant Coordinator, for Psychosocial Assessment for Heart Transplant Evaluation.     Information for this assessment was obtained through an interview with the patient, patient's mother, ******** *******, and review of the medical records. SW spent approximately 60 minutes of face-to-face time with patient and family.     Living situation:  **, ****, resides with his mother, stepfather, and brother in ********, *******. They reside at **** * ******** *******, ********, ** *****. They **** a 2-bedroom ******* with central a/c and heat. They change their air filter only once every 6 months. They have well water. Both adults smoke in the home and in the car[SM1].  They have three dogs that are both inside and outside, two pit bulls and a *********.      Demographics:  Mother:  ******** *******  ***:  **/**/****  Language: English   Education Level: 11th Grade          Employment:  CNA at Osprey Point Nursing Home               Phone:  ***-***-****     Stepfather: ******* *******  Mom declined to give telephone number     Siblings in Home:  ***** ***** 17      Social History and Support Systems:  **** lives with his mother, stepfather, and brother in ********, **. ******** and ******* have been married for 10 years. ****'s biological father resides in **** and has minimal involvement/contact. They have limited social support. The only person other than ******* that mom was able to name *** ******* *** *** daughter (24) that resides in Inverness. They are not involved in any church or community support groups. Mom plans to be ****'s primary caregiver post-transplant but this would require her to quit work.         **** is enrolled in the 9th grade special education program at ****** **** ******. He has an IEP in place.  She denies any diagnosis of developmental delay. Until this school year, he received PT and OT. Mom says this ended due to him being moved to high school. **** has been diagnosed with PTSD, ADHD, Bipolar disorder, and OCD. He is not under the care of a psychologist or psychiatrist. At one time, he was prescribed Risperidone but mom took him off the medication because she felt it was causing gynecomastia. She did not take him off under physician supervision. **** enjoys playing Xbox and drawing. Neither **** nor mom feel that he is limited by his illness at this time. However, they later stated that he has not been able to go to school and has lost 30-40lbs during this last month due to being ill.   Mom denies any objections to blood products, transfusions, etc.     Course of illness:     **** ***** is a 16 y/o male with a presumed history of ******'s Muscular Dystrophy. He was transferred from ***** General Hospital due to worsening heart failure due to dilated cardiomyopathy associated with ******'s muscular dystrophy. He was admitted with a one-month history of vomiting and fatigue. In the ER, it was noticed that his EF was ~25%. Milrinone therapy was initiated. He was then transferred to ** ****** for further management of heart failure and evaluation for heart transplant.     Financial situation:  ******** is employed full time as a CNA. She has been at *** ******* ***** of employment for only two months. She works 5 days per week. She is not yet eligible for benefits. So far, her employer has been understanding of her situation. **** receives social security disability for his diagnosis of ******'s Muscular Dystrophy as well as bipolar disorder. ******* also receives a disability check.   There will be a significant loss of income with the transplant process. If ******* is hospitalized, his disability check will be significantly decreased. Mom was informed of this. Mom also plans to quit work to be the primary caregiver post-transplant. They are unable to survive financially on *******'s disability check alone. SW discussed the possibility of starting to save now while still able to work. Mom was unable to answer on whether there was income available for this at this time. Fundraising would be difficult for family due to limited social network.   **** is covered by ******** Medicaid. This will cover all medical expenses at 100%.  Mom has one vehicle and reports that transportation will not be a barrier.      Family History:  Mom disclosed a remote history of depression with suicide attempt as a teenager. **** has been diagnosed with PTSD, ADHD, bipolar disorder, and OCD. He is not under the care of a psychologist or psychiatrist.   Mom reports that ******* has a history of criminal charges. She thinks they were drug related but cannot recall. It was approximately 15 years ago.  There is a significant history of domestic violence between mom and ****'s biological father. When **** and his brother were 3 and 4, the father seriously injured mom and DCF became involved. They removed the children due to failure to protect. They were ********* a month and a half later. Mom ***** insight as to why the children were removed. She stated to SW, 'I didn't fail to protect my kids; he beat the **** out of me, not them.'   ******* uses *********, mom reports that he has now been approved for medical use.      Adherence:  There are significant concerns for adherence due to past medical records. He has not been seen by an MD specialist since 2009. He has not been taking cardiac medications prescribed since 2016. He has been lost to follow up to several providers. He is not under the care of a psychologist or psychiatrist. Mom has stopped medications without consulting with physicians.  SW discussed the importance of medications after transplant and the red flags (noncompliance) in patient's chart. Mom reports that she would never stop or make changes to medications post-transplant. SW inquired about specific ********** of noncompliance. Mom reports that he was not taking the Lisinopril due to being unable to afford to drive to the doctor's office. SW discussed the option of using Medicaid transportation to get to and from appointments. Mom reports that she was unaware of this. SW also reminded her that she had disclosed that she stopped his risperidone without the doctor. She did not respond to this.      Assessment and recommendations:  Mom was unable to remain awake and alert during interview. SW had scheduled 9am meeting time with mom per mom's request. Mom was asleep at the time of SW arrival. SW awoke mom and had to continue awaking mom after each question asked. Information was limited due to this as well as mom's guardedness. SW is concerned as there have been similar reports from other practitioners that have met with mom throughout different and later times in the day.    Family has limited support. Without mom's income as well as ****'s social security check, the family cannot survive financially. However, there is no one else that mom can identify to assist in ****'s care. SW is also very concerned due to the significant history of noncompliance. Family has been lost to follow up. Mom has discontinued medication on several occasions without physician knowledge or supervision. ****, while 16 years old, is developmentally delayed and unable to care for himself.   Psychology has also met with and evaluated patient and family. Mom more actively participated in their interview but still fell asleep and had to be awoken ************. (Please also see psychology consult from **/**.) During the interview there was found to be a more complex DCF history than what was reported to SW. Mom also informed that ******* was arrested recently for having methamphetamine in the **** on their property. They are in the process of being evicted from their home due to this finding/arrest. Mom was recently fired from a job of 10 years due to suspicion of drug use and positive drug screen. **** admitted to marijuana use. He also admitted to frequent truancy from school.   SW provided mom with copy of transplant compliance contracts. DCF may need to be involved asap due to medical neglect and inability to proceed with transplant in current home.         IMPRESSION:     (Low Risk - 1; Moderate Risk - 2; High Risk - 3; Severe Risk - 4)     Home Environment/Transportation -  4     Family Background & Social Support -  4     Financial/Insurance - 3     Mental Health/Substance Abuse - 4     Involvement with *** Enforcement/Child Protection -  4     Adherence -4     Understanding of medical situation & transplant process - 4     Health Literacy -  2     Coping Skills - 3     Total:  32 Severe Risk     The family scores as Severe risk in regards to psychosocial contra-indicators to transplant.          Recommendations:  *Complete Pre and Post-Transplant Contracts with Family to address concerns with adherence.  *Provide continuing education to the family about heart transplant and post-transplant care.  *Arrange for ********* to work with **** regarding transplant education.  *Assist family with financial plan and caregiving plan for transplant.  *Offer support and guidance to family as needed.  *Monitor compliance.   *Discuss DCF report with team due to medical neglect and inability to proceed with transplant in current home.            ******** *****, LCSW  Pediatric Heart and Lung Transplant Team  ***-***-****[SM1]smoking
